Решето компиляторов

Вы узнаете

Каких компиляторов отсеивает таблица из десяти вопросов и почему «неизвестно» не смешивают с «нет».

Решето задаёт 10 вопросов 9 компиляторам: доказана ли корректность, проверяет ли валидатор, проверен ли против другой реализации, пересобран ли из независимого бутстрапа, есть ли эталонный интерпретатор, измерен ли прогрев, опубликована ли скорость, переориентируем ли, воспроизводима ли сборка и учитываются ли пустые проходы. Клетка — истина, ложь, неизвестно или неприменимо, и отсеивает компилятор только ложь. Для 7 сторонних компиляторов клетка ложна, только если так сказано в источнике, и по приведённым данным не отсеян ни один. У t27c 4 ложные клетки, а у t27b 1, потому что для них источник — мы сами. Между 2026-10-05 и 2026-10-09 4 клетки сменились с ложи на истину.

Попробовать

Выберите t27c и C9 и прочитайте задачу с исправлением. Потом покажите строки на 2026-10-05 и посчитайте ложные клетки в строке t27c.

Открыть интерактивный урок →

Ten yes-or-no questions asked of nine compilers, with unknown kept apart from no. Pick a compiler, a filter and a date of the t27 rows, and see the cell, its fix issue and what the filter removes.

specs/compiler/theory/sieve.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/theory/sieve.t27 -- the compiler sieve: ten filters, nine candidates, and the golden
; reference language derived from what passes them (gHashTag/t27 epic #6488, issue #6502).
; ASCII only (L3).

; The owner's order (2026-10-05, translated): compare compilers and draw the conclusions as theorems,
; in the style of the TNF work, toward the task of building a golden reference programming language.
; The TNF style (specs/numeric, the GOLDEN SIEVE): each filter is a decidable predicate, each cell is
; sourced, and the theorems say which filters actually remove a candidate, which are subsumed by
; others, which never fire, and who survives.

; ---- Values -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; A cell is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN (Kleene: FALSE = 0, UNKNOWN = 1, TRUE = 2), or NA when the filter's
; predicate does not apply (a JIT-warmup filter on an ahead-of-time compiler; a self-hosting filter on
; a backend). Rules:
; - UNKNOWN when no opened source states the cell. Never a guess.
; - Only FALSE removes a candidate. NA and UNKNOWN never do.
; - For an external candidate, a cell is FALSE only if a source says so. For t27c and t27b we are the
;   source: a missing capability we know is missing is FALSE. This asymmetry is deliberate and is the
;   reason the theorems below may not be read as "t27 is worse than X"; they say where t27 is KNOWN
;   to fall short, and how little is known about the others.

; ---- The filters (each a predicate on one compiler or backend) ----------------------------------
; C1 semantic preservation is PROVED for the compiler (machine-checked).
;    X. Leroy, "Formal verification of a realistic compiler", CACM 52(7):107-115, 2009,
;    DOI 10.1145/1538788.1538814. R. Kumar, M. O. Myreen, M. Norrish, S. Owens, "CakeML: a verified
;    implementation of ML", POPL 2014, DOI 10.1145/2535838.2535841.
; C2 a translation VALIDATOR checks individual compilations (any pass; partial counts as TRUE).
;    A. Pnueli, M. Siegel, E. Singerman, "Translation validation", TACAS 1998, LNCS 1384:151-166,
;    DOI 10.1007/BFb0054170. G. C. Necula, "Translation validation for an optimizing compiler",
;    PLDI 2000:83-94, DOI 10.1145/349299.349314.
; C3 DIFFERENTIAL testing against an independent implementation, per test, with generated programs
;    or a per-backend test matrix compared against a reference backend.
;    W. M. McKeeman, Digital Technical Journal 10(1):100-107, 1998 (record only, text UNVERIFIED).
;    X. Yang, Y. Chen, E. Eide, J. Regehr, PLDI 2011, DOI 10.1145/1993498.1993532 (Csmith).
;    V. Le, M. Afshari, Z. Su, PLDI 2014, DOI 10.1145/2594291.2594334 (EMI).
;    V. Livinskii, D. Babokin, J. Regehr, OOPSLA 2020, DOI 10.1145/3428264 (YARPGen).
; C4 the self-hosting toolchain is rebuilt bit-identically from an INDEPENDENT bootstrap compiler
;    (Diverse Double-Compiling or an equivalent). NA for a backend that is not a toolchain.
;    K. Thompson, CACM 27(8):761-763, 1984, DOI 10.1145/358198.358210. D. A. Wheeler, ACSAC 2005,
;    pp. 28-40, and PhD dissertation, George Mason University, 2009.
; C5 an executable REFERENCE INTERPRETER exists and is used as an oracle against compiled code.
;    Y. Futamura, Higher-Order and Symbolic Computation 12(4):381-391, 1999,
;    DOI 10.1023/A:1010095604496 (the first projection's wording behind the paywall: UNVERIFIED).
; C6 JIT warmup is MEASURED (steady state per benchmark, not assumed). NA for ahead-of-time.
;    E. Barrett, C. F. Bolz-Tereick, R. Killick, S. Mount, L. Tratt, "Virtual machine warmup blows
;    hot and cold", OOPSLA 2017, DOI 10.1145/3133876: at most 43.5% of (VM, benchmark) pairs
;    consistently reach a steady state of peak performance.
; C7 compile speed and code quality are PUBLISHED as numbers against a reference compiler.
;    SPEC CPU 2017 (spec.org/cpu2017). H. Xu, F. Kjolstad, "Copy-and-patch compilation", OOPSLA 2021,
;    DOI 10.1145/3485513.
; C8 RETARGETABLE: more than one target from one middle end. NA for a backend that names one ISA.
;    C. W. Fraser, D. R. Hanson, "A Retargetable C Compiler", Addison-Wesley 1995 (lcc).
;    N. Ramsey, M. F. Fernandez, TOPLAS 19(3):492-524, 1997, DOI 10.1145/256167.256225.
; C9 REPRODUCIBLE build: the same source, environment and instructions give bit-identical artifacts.
;    reproducible-builds.org/docs/definition. C. Lamb, S. Zacchiroli, IEEE Software 39(2):62-70,
;    2022, DOI 10.1109/MS.2021.3073045.
; C10 VACUITY-AWARE test accounting: a pass with no executed check is not counted as coverage.
;    I. Beer, S. Ben-David, C. Eisner, Y. Rodeh, CAV 1997, LNCS 1254:279-290,
;    DOI 10.1007/3-540-63166-6_28 ("vacuous pass"). Y. Jia, M. Harman, IEEE TSE 37(5):649-678, 2011,
;    DOI 10.1109/TSE.2010.62 (mutation adequacy).

; ---- The cells, with their sources (opened 2026-10-05; t27c and t27b re-read 2026-10-07) -------

;     "passing 1987 behavior tests, versus 1980 passed by the LLVM backend".
;   C7 TRUE: devlog 2025-06-08 (hello.zig 275 ms vs 918 ms with -fllvm); 2025-07-23 (aarch64).
;   C9 TRUE for the toolchain (ziglang.org/news/goodbye-cpp: zig3 and zig4 identical byte for byte);

;   C4 NA, C6 NA (AOT), C8 NA (one ISA each). C1, C2, C5, C10 UNKNOWN.
; rustc_codegen_cranelift (cg_clif):
;   C2 TRUE partial: the regalloc checker (cfallin.org/blog/2021/03/15/cranelift-isel-3).
;   C3 TRUE: Rustlantis, OOPSLA 2024 (ralfj.de/blog/2024/11/25/rustlantis.html) compares backends.

;   C7 TRUE: lwn.net/Articles/964735 (29.6 s vs 37.5 s with LLVM). C8 TRUE: README target matrix.
;   C4 NA. C1, C6, C9, C10 UNKNOWN.
; Go gc SSA backend:
;   C4 TRUE: go.dev/blog/rebuild (any bootstrap, back to Go 1.4's C implementation, gives the same
;     toolchain); C9 TRUE: same page, Go 1.21.0 "perfectly reproducible builds".
;   C7 TRUE: go.dev/doc/go1.7 (5-35% CPU time). C8 TRUE: go.dev/doc/install/source port list.
;   C6 NA. C1, C2, C3, C5, C10 UNKNOWN.
; QBE:
;   C7 TRUE: c9x.me/compile ("70% of the performance of industrial optimizing compilers in 10% of
;     the code"). C8 TRUE: amd64, arm64, riscv64. C9 TRUE: tests.reproducible-builds.org (Debian).
;   C3 UNKNOWN: tools/test.sh compares against expected output, not a reference backend.
;   C4 NA, C6 NA. C1, C2, C5, C10 UNKNOWN.
; CompCert:
;   C1 TRUE: compcert.org/compcert-C.html ("each of the transformation passes is proved to preserve
;     semantics"; parser, assembler and linker unverified).
;   C2 TRUE partial: register allocation validated a posteriori (source overview; Leroy POPL 2006 was
;     seen in search only, so this cell rests on the CompCert overview).
;   C3 TRUE: Csmith (PLDI 2011) found wrong code only in unverified front-end parts.
;   C7 TRUE: compcert-C.html (about 90% of GCC -O1 on ARMv8). C8 TRUE: PowerPC, ARM, RISC-V, x86.
;   C4 NA (not self-hosting), C6 NA. C5 UNKNOWN (the interpreter exists, use as oracle not stated),
;   C9 UNKNOWN, C10 UNKNOWN.
; LLVM:
;   C2 TRUE partial: Alive2 validates IR-level transformations (github.com/AliveToolkit/alive2).
;   C3 TRUE: Csmith (PLDI 2011), Rustlantis (12 LLVM-backend bugs).
;   C7 TRUE as the baseline of others' published numbers. C8 TRUE: llvm.org/docs/CompilerWriterInfo.
;   C9 TRUE partial: tests.reproducible-builds.org, llvm-toolchain-19 reproducible on trixie amd64.
;   C1, C4, C5, C6, C10 UNKNOWN.
; t27c (bootstrap/src) -- our own knowledge. Opened at master 682564f48 (2026-10-05) with seven
; FALSE cells; re-read at master 17e01d205 (2026-10-07, #7597) once every fix issue T741 named had

; recorded with the rule in specs/compiler/theory/reproducible.t27.
;   C1 FALSE (no mechanised semantics). #6446 made gen refuse what typecheck refuses; that proves

;   C2 TRUE partial (was FALSE): since #6441 (PR #6530) the verdict of every test t27c compiles and

; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module CompilerTheorySieve;

pub const FALSE3 : u8 = 0;
pub const UNKNOWN3 : u8 = 1;
pub const TRUE3 : u8 = 2;
pub const NA3 : u8 = 3;

pub const ZIG_A64 : u32 = 0;
pub const ZIG_X86 : u32 = 1;
pub const CG_CLIF : u32 = 2;
pub const GO_SSA : u32 = 3;
pub const QBE : u32 = 4;
pub const COMPCERT : u32 = 5;
pub const LLVM : u32 = 6;
pub const T27C : u32 = 7;
pub const T27B : u32 = 8;
pub const CANDIDATES : u32 = 9;
pub const EXTERNAL : u32 = 7;

pub const C1 : u32 = 1;
pub const C2 : u32 = 2;
pub const C3 : u32 = 3;
pub const C4 : u32 = 4;
pub const C5 : u32 = 5;
pub const C6 : u32 = 6;
pub const C7 : u32 = 7;
pub const C8 : u32 = 8;
pub const C9 : u32 = 9;
pub const C10 : u32 = 10;
pub const FILTERS : u32 = 10;

; Kleene conjunction and negation on FALSE < UNKNOWN < TRUE (NA is read as TRUE: it never removes).
pub fn as_kleene(v: u8) -> u8 {
    if (v == NA3) { return TRUE3; }
    return v;
}

pub fn k_and(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
    var x : u8 = as_kleene(a);
    var y : u8 = as_kleene(b);
    if (x < y) { return x; }
    return y;
}

pub fn k_not(a: u8) -> u8 {
    return TRUE3 - as_kleene(a);
}

pub fn cell_zig(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return NA3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_cg_clif(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C5) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_go(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C4) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_qbe(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_compcert(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C1) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_llvm(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return TRUE3; }
    return UNKNOWN3;
}

pub fn cell_t27c(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C10) { return TRUE3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

pub fn cell_t27b(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C5) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C6) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C7) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C10) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return NA3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

; The two rows as they stood at master be9757784 (2026-10-09), before #7596 measured warmup and
; published speed and quality and #8148 measured C9; T752 and T741 check what those moved.
pub fn cell_t27c_at_be9757784(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return UNKNOWN3; }
    if (f == C10) { return TRUE3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

pub fn cell_t27b_at_be9757784(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C3) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C5) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C10) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C9) { return UNKNOWN3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

; The two rows as they stood at master 682564f48 (2026-10-05), kept so that T741's account of what
; the closed fix issues moved is checked by a test rather than asserted in prose.
pub fn cell_t27c_at_682564f48(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C6) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C9) { return UNKNOWN3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

pub fn cell_t27b_at_682564f48(f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (f == C2) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C5) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C10) { return TRUE3; }
    if (f == C4) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C8) { return NA3; }
    if (f == C9) { return UNKNOWN3; }
    return FALSE3;
}

pub fn value(c: u32, f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (c == ZIG_A64) { return cell_zig(f); }
    if (c == ZIG_X86) { return cell_zig(f); }
    if (c == CG_CLIF) { return cell_cg_clif(f); }
    if (c == GO_SSA) { return cell_go(f); }
    if (c == QBE) { return cell_qbe(f); }
    if (c == COMPCERT) { return cell_compcert(f); }
    if (c == LLVM) { return cell_llvm(f); }
    if (c == T27C) { return cell_t27c(f); }
    return cell_t27b(f);
}

; The candidates filter f removes, as a bit mask over the nine candidates.
pub fn kills(f: u32) -> u32 {
    var c : u32 = 0;
    var m : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        if (value(c, f) == FALSE3) { m = m | (1 << c); }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    return m;
}

; A candidate's verdict over all ten filters (Kleene AND of every cell).
pub fn verdict(c: u32) -> u8 {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var v : u8 = TRUE3;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        v = k_and(v, value(c, f));
        f = f + 1;
    }
    return v;
}

pub fn count_bits(m: u32) -> u32 {
    var x : u32 = m;
    var n : u32 = 0;
    while (x != 0) {
        n = n + (x & 1);
        x = x >> 1;
    }
    return n;
}

pub fn cells_with(c: u32, v: u8) -> u32 {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var n : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        if (value(c, f) == v) { n = n + 1; }
        f = f + 1;
    }
    return n;
}

; Filters whose kill set lies inside filter g's: g subsumes them.
pub fn subsumed_by(g: u32) -> u32 {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var n : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        if (f != g) {
            if ((kills(f) & (kills(g) ^ 511)) == 0) { n = n + 1; }
        }
        f = f + 1;
    }
    return n;
}

; Candidates killed by filter f and by no other filter.
pub fn unique_kills(f: u32) -> u32 {
    var others : u32 = 0;
    var g : u32 = 1;
    while (g <= FILTERS) {
        if (g != f) { others = others | kills(g); }
        g = g + 1;
    }
    return kills(f) & (others ^ 511);
}

pub const BIT_T27C : u32 = 128;
pub const BIT_T27B : u32 = 256;

; ==================================================================================================
; T737 -- on published evidence the sieve removes no external candidate.
; Statement. No opened source states a FALSE cell for Zig aarch64, Zig x86_64, cg_clif, Go SSA, QBE,
; CompCert or LLVM, so every filter's kill set lies inside {t27c, t27b}. Proof: the table; the test
; counts it. Reading: the sieve as published cannot rank the external field; its ranking power comes
; only from cells we know about ourselves (see the asymmetry rule above).
; ==================================================================================================

test t737_no_external_candidate_is_removed {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var outside : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        outside = outside | (kills(f) & 127);
        f = f + 1;
    }
    assert outside == 0;
    var c : u32 = 0;
    var false_cells : u32 = 0;
    while (c < EXTERNAL) {
        false_cells = false_cells + cells_with(c, FALSE3);
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert false_cells == 0;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T738 -- no candidate survives strictly; seven survive possibly; t27c and t27b are removed.
; Statement. Strict survival (every cell TRUE or NA) holds for no candidate, because C10 is UNKNOWN
; for all seven external candidates: no opened source addresses zero-assert passes for any of them.
; Possible survival (no FALSE cell) holds exactly for the seven external candidates. t27c is
; removed by four filters (C1, C4, C5, C9), t27b by one (C1). (At 682564f48 the counts were seven
; and four, at be9757784 four and three; T741 and T752 say what moved them.) Proof: Kleene AND per
; row.
; ==================================================================================================

test t738_survivors {
    var c : u32 = 0;
    var strict : u32 = 0;
    var possible : u32 = 0;
    var c10_unknown : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        if (verdict(c) == TRUE3) { strict = strict + 1; }
        if (verdict(c) != FALSE3) { possible = possible + 1; }
        if (c < EXTERNAL) {
            if (value(c, C10) == UNKNOWN3) { c10_unknown = c10_unknown + 1; }
        }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert strict == 0;
    assert possible == EXTERNAL;
    assert c10_unknown == EXTERNAL;
    assert verdict(T27C) == FALSE3;
    assert verdict(T27B) == FALSE3;
    assert cells_with(T27C, FALSE3) == 4;
    assert cells_with(T27B, FALSE3) == 1;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T739 -- one filter wearing four (the T441 analog).
; Statement. Four of the ten filters fire; C2 (translation validation), C3 (differential testing),
; C6 (warmup), C7 (speed and quality), C8 (retargetability) and C10 (vacuity) never fire. C1
; (proved preservation) removes both t27c and t27b, and the kill set of every other filter lies
; inside C1's: C1 alone does all the removing, and the other three firing filters are subsumed by
; it. C1 is now the only filter that removes t27b, so it has one unique kill, {t27b}. The distinct
; kill sets are two: {t27c, t27b} (C1) and {t27c} (C4, C5, C9). At 682564f48 eight filters fired;
; #6441, #6442, #6445 and #6509 silenced C2, C3 and C10, #7596 (T752) silenced C6 and C7, and
; #8148 measured C9, which fires on t27c alone (T741). Reading: as a sieve, the ten filters collapse to one; as a GAP LIST
; they do not collapse, because each FALSE has a different fix (T741).
; ==================================================================================================

test t739_which_filters_fire {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var firing : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        if (kills(f) != 0) { firing = firing + 1; }
        f = f + 1;
    }
    assert firing == 4;
    assert kills(C2) == 0;
    assert kills(C3) == 0;
    assert kills(C8) == 0;
    assert kills(C9) == BIT_T27C;
    assert kills(C10) == 0;
    assert kills(C6) == 0;
    assert kills(C7) == 0;
    assert kills(C1) == (BIT_T27C | BIT_T27B);
    assert kills(C4) == BIT_T27C;
    assert kills(C5) == BIT_T27C;
}

test t739_c1_subsumes_every_filter_and_alone_removes_t27b {
    assert subsumed_by(C1) == 9;
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var unique : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        unique = unique | unique_kills(f);
        f = f + 1;
    }
    assert unique == BIT_T27B;
    assert unique_kills(C1) == BIT_T27B;
    assert unique_kills(C4) == 0;
    assert unique_kills(C9) == 0;
    assert subsumed_by(C6) == 5;
}

; Negative control: a candidate with one FALSE among TRUE cells is removed, and with the FALSE made
; UNKNOWN it is not; NA never removes.
test t739_negative_control_one_false_removes {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var v : u8 = TRUE3;
    var w : u8 = TRUE3;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        if (f == C4) {
            v = k_and(v, FALSE3);
            w = k_and(w, UNKNOWN3);
        } else {
            v = k_and(v, NA3);
            w = k_and(w, TRUE3);
        }
        f = f + 1;
    }
    assert v == FALSE3;
    assert w == UNKNOWN3;
    assert k_not(UNKNOWN3) == UNKNOWN3;
    assert k_not(FALSE3) == TRUE3;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T740 -- what t27 knows that the field does not publish.
; Statement. t27c and t27b both hold TRUE on C10 (vacuity-aware accounting), a cell that is UNKNOWN
; for every external candidate (t27c since #6509); t27c holds TRUE on C8 like five external
; candidates; t27b holds TRUE on C9 (reproducible builds, #8148) like Zig, Go, QBE and LLVM. t27c is
; known TRUE on five filters and t27b on seven, against at most five for an external candidate
; (CompCert, cg_clif and LLVM: five each). The lead is the asymmetry rule above,
; not a ranking: our own cells are read from our own runs, theirs only from what they publish.
; Proof: the table.
; ==================================================================================================

test t740_known_cells {
    var c : u32 = 0;
    var best : u32 = 0;
    var c10_true : u32 = 0;
    var c8_true : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        var t : u32 = cells_with(c, TRUE3);
        if (t > best) { best = t; }
        if (value(c, C10) == TRUE3) { c10_true = c10_true + 1; }
        if (value(c, C8) == TRUE3) { c8_true = c8_true + 1; }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert best == 7;
    assert cells_with(COMPCERT, TRUE3) == 5;
    assert cells_with(CG_CLIF, TRUE3) == 5;
    assert cells_with(LLVM, TRUE3) == 5;
    assert cells_with(T27C, TRUE3) == 5;
    assert cells_with(T27B, TRUE3) == 7;
    assert value(T27B, C9) == TRUE3;
    assert c10_true == 2;
    assert value(T27B, C10) == TRUE3;
    assert value(T27C, C10) == TRUE3;
    assert c8_true == 6;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T741 -- every FALSE cell of t27 has a fixing issue.
; Statement. Each of the five FALSE cells of t27c and t27b maps to an open issue in gHashTag/t27
; that, when closed, turns it to TRUE or states why it stays FALSE:
;   C1 -> #7595 (a mechanised semantics of a t27 subset and a preservation proof for one backend)
;   C4, C5 (t27c) -> #5980 (the self-hosted core: a front end that does not share compiler.rs, so
;         DDC becomes independent -- a signed DDC receipt saying DDC_INDEPENDENT, #7699 -- and a
;         second path to the source's meaning)
;   C9 (t27c) -> #8178 (a fixed-length git identity in build.rs and the CARGO_HOME path remapped,
;         measured to give one t27c across two cache paths and both labs, reproducible.t27)
; #7596 (measured warmup; compile speed and code quality published against a reference compiler)
; was the fix issue of t27b C6 and of C7 for both; it turned all three TRUE (T752).
; History. At 682564f48 there were eleven FALSE cells, mapped to #6446, #6441, #6442, #6445, #6508,
; #6444 and #6509. All seven issues closed by 2026-10-07. Four cells turned TRUE because the gap
; their text named was closed: t27c C2 and C3 and t27b C3 (#6441, #6442, #6445) and t27c C10
; (#6509). Three issues closed without turning their cell, and each says why: #6446 proves no
; preservation (C1), #6508's DDC shares a front end (T729, C4), #6444 gave runners, not numbers (C6,
; C7). No cell moved the other way. From be9757784 to now, besides T752's three C6 and C7 cells,
; only C9 moved, both cells from UNKNOWN: #8148 measured t27b TRUE and t27c FALSE, which adds #8178.
; Proof: the function below is total on the FALSE cells, and the 682564f48 and be9757784 rows count
; the moves (the tests: 682564f48 -> be9757784 and the C9 move here, C6 and C7 in T752).
; ==================================================================================================

pub fn fix_issue(c: u32, f: u32) -> u32 {
    if (value(c, f) != FALSE3) { return 0; }
    if (f == C1) { return 7595; }
    if (f == C4) { return 5980; }
    if (f == C5) { return 5980; }
    if (f == C9) { return 8178; }
    return 0;
}

; The 682564f48 value of a t27 cell (t27c or t27b only).
pub fn value_at_682564f48(c: u32, f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (c == T27C) { return cell_t27c_at_682564f48(f); }
    return cell_t27b_at_682564f48(f);
}

; The be9757784 value of a t27 cell (t27c or t27b only).
pub fn value_at_be9757784(c: u32, f: u32) -> u8 {
    if (c == T27C) { return cell_t27c_at_be9757784(f); }
    return cell_t27b_at_be9757784(f);
}

test t741_the_closed_fix_issues_moved_four_cells_and_none_back {
    var c : u32 = T27C;
    var before : u32 = 0;
    var after : u32 = 0;
    var false_to_true : u32 = 0;
    var moves : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        var f : u32 = 1;
        while (f <= FILTERS) {
            var then_v : u8 = value_at_682564f48(c, f);
            var now_v : u8 = value_at_be9757784(c, f);
            if (then_v == FALSE3) { before = before + 1; }
            if (now_v == FALSE3) { after = after + 1; }
            if (then_v != now_v) { moves = moves + 1; }
            if (then_v == FALSE3) {
                if (now_v == TRUE3) { false_to_true = false_to_true + 1; }
            }
            f = f + 1;
        }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert before == 11;
    assert after == 7;
    assert false_to_true == 4;
    assert moves == false_to_true;
    assert value_at_682564f48(T27C, C2) == FALSE3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27C, C2) == TRUE3;
    assert value_at_682564f48(T27C, C10) == FALSE3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27C, C10) == TRUE3;
    assert value_at_682564f48(T27B, C3) == FALSE3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27B, C3) == TRUE3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27C, C4) == FALSE3;
}

test t741_the_c9_measurement_moved_two_unknown_cells_and_nothing_else {
    var c : u32 = T27C;
    var moves : u32 = 0;
    var c9_moves : u32 = 0;
    var from_unknown : u32 = 0;
    var outside : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        var f : u32 = 1;
        while (f <= FILTERS) {
            var then_v : u8 = value_at_be9757784(c, f);
            var now_v : u8 = value(c, f);
            if (then_v != now_v) {
                moves = moves + 1;
                if (f == C9) {
                    c9_moves = c9_moves + 1;
                    if (then_v == UNKNOWN3) { from_unknown = from_unknown + 1; }
                } else {
                    if (f != C6) {
                        if (f != C7) { outside = outside + 1; }
                    }
                }
            }
            f = f + 1;
        }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert moves == 5;
    assert c9_moves == 2;
    assert from_unknown == 2;
    assert outside == 0;
    assert value(T27C, C9) == FALSE3;
    assert value(T27B, C9) == TRUE3;
    assert fix_issue(T27C, C9) == 8178;
    assert fix_issue(T27B, C9) == 0;
}

test t741_every_t27_false_cell_has_an_issue {
    var c : u32 = T27C;
    var falses : u32 = 0;
    var unmapped : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        var f : u32 = 1;
        while (f <= FILTERS) {
            if (value(c, f) == FALSE3) {
                falses = falses + 1;
                if (fix_issue(c, f) == 0) { unmapped = unmapped + 1; }
            }
            f = f + 1;
        }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert falses == 5;
    assert unmapped == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27B, C10) == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27C, C10) == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27C, C3) == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27C, C4) == 5980;
    assert fix_issue(T27B, C6) == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27C, C7) == 0;
    assert fix_issue(T27B, C1) == 7595;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T752 -- #7596 measured warmup and published speed and quality: three cells moved, FALSE to TRUE.
; Statement. Between master be9757784 and this row, t27b C6, t27b C7 and t27c C7 turned TRUE, and no
; other C6 or C7 cell moved; t27c C6 stays NA (ahead-of-time). The evidence is three specs, each with
; its own tests:
;   specs/compiler/theory/warmup.t27 (T750) -- the Barrett et al. 2017 classifier (outliers, optimal
;     partitioning on mean and variance, the steady-state rule, the per-benchmark class), checked
;     on synthetic series that must come out flat, warmup, slowdown, no steady state;
;   specs/compiler/theory/warmup_t27b.t27 (T751) -- the 30000 iteration times of the lab run,
;     classified by T750: 3 FLAT, 2 GOOD INCONSISTENT, 1 BAD INCONSISTENT;
;   specs/compiler/theory/speed_quality.t27 (T753) -- compile and run samples for t27b and for t27c
;     through gcc, clang and zig, with the published medians and geomeans recomputed by its tests.
; Report: docs/reports/2026-10-09-sieve-c6-c7.md. Limits, stated where the cells are: every run was
; aarch64 under qemu on the shared x86 lab, not native arm64; the six kernels of specs/benchmarks.
; Only C6 and C7 are counted here, so a move of another filter is T741's or its own theorem's.
; ==================================================================================================

test t752_warmup_and_speed_moved_three_cells_false_to_true {
    var c : u32 = T27C;
    var moves : u32 = 0;
    var false_to_true : u32 = 0;
    while (c < CANDIDATES) {
        var f : u32 = C6;
        while (f <= C7) {
            var then_v : u8 = value_at_be9757784(c, f);
            var now_v : u8 = value(c, f);
            if (then_v != now_v) { moves = moves + 1; }
            if (then_v == FALSE3) {
                if (now_v == TRUE3) { false_to_true = false_to_true + 1; }
            }
            f = f + 1;
        }
        c = c + 1;
    }
    assert moves == 3;
    assert false_to_true == 3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27B, C6) == FALSE3;
    assert value(T27B, C6) == TRUE3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27C, C7) == FALSE3;
    assert value(T27C, C7) == TRUE3;
    assert value(T27B, C7) == TRUE3;
    assert value(T27C, C6) == NA3;
    assert value_at_be9757784(T27C, C6) == NA3;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T742 -- the golden reference language.
; Definition. A language is a golden reference when its toolchain passes every filter: each filter
; below becomes a property the language and its toolchain must have. T-status for t27 today:
; PRESENT (shipped and checked), PARTIAL (exists with a stated limit), MISSING.
;   G1 (C1)  a mechanised semantics and a preservation proof of the compiler ............ MISSING
;   G2 (C2)  every compilation of a test validated against a reference .................. PARTIAL
;            (per test, t27b checks codegen against its IR by value, and t27c's verdict is checked
;            against t27b's, #6441; neither is checked against the meaning of the t27 source)
;   G3 (C3)  an independent second implementation compared per test, plus a program generator
;            and a reducer ......................................................... PARTIAL
;            (per-test compare #6441, generator #6442 and reducer #6445 exist; the front end is
;            shared, T729, so the second implementation is a second backend only)
;   G4 (C4)  a self-hosted compiler rebuilt identically from an independent bootstrap ..... PARTIAL
;            (t27core fixpoint exists; DDC runs and agrees, T732, but its routes share a front end)
;   G5 (C5)  an executable reference interpreter of the SOURCE, used as the oracle ........ PARTIAL
;            (eval.rs interprets the IR, not the source)
;   G6 (C6, C7) measured warmup, compile speed and code quality, published .............. PARTIAL
;            (was MISSING: #7596 measured and published both, T752; one run, aarch64 under qemu,
;            six kernels, not tracked per commit)
;   G7 (C8)  many targets from one middle end ........................................ PRESENT
;   G8 (C9)  bit-identical builds of the toolchain ................................... PARTIAL
;            (t27b builds bit-identical and gen, gen-c, gen-rust are deterministic, #8148; t27c's
;            build carries the git abbreviation and the CARGO_HOME path, #8178)
;   G9 (C10) vacuity-aware accounting on every test path ............................. PARTIAL
;            (t27b corpus, #6115, and t27c test-report, #6509; other runners, such as `t27c
;            suite`, are not shown to be vacuity-aware)
;   G10 (T735) machine encodings that round-trip, so backend blame is decidable ........ PARTIAL
;            (was MISSING: 5 of 47 TRI-27 opcodes failed. The t27a field table round-trips all 47,
;            T736, and ships as `t27c asm` / `t27c disasm`, #6507; that every producer of TRI-27
;            words uses it is not shown)
; Statement (re-read 2026-10-09). t27 has 1 property present, 8 partial and 1 missing (it was 1, 6
; and 3 at 682564f48, and 1, 7 and 2 at be9757784: G10, then G6 moved). No candidate of the sieve is
; known to have all ten: G9 is unknown for every external candidate (T738), and G1 is known only
; for CompCert. Golden is therefore a direction, not a membership: the order in which t27 closes
; the gaps is the issue order of T741.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const ST_MISSING : u8 = 0;
pub const ST_PARTIAL : u8 = 1;
pub const ST_PRESENT : u8 = 2;
pub const GOLDEN : u32 = 10;

pub fn t27_status(g: u32) -> u8 {
    if (g == 1) { return ST_MISSING; }
    if (g == 7) { return ST_PRESENT; }
    return ST_PARTIAL;
}

; The sieve filter a golden property comes from (0 for G10, which comes from T735).
pub fn golden_filter(g: u32) -> u32 {
    if (g <= 5) { return g; }
    if (g == 6) { return C6; }
    if (g == 10) { return 0; }
    return g + 1;
}

test t742_t27_against_the_golden_language {
    var g : u32 = 1;
    var present : u32 = 0;
    var partial : u32 = 0;
    var missing : u32 = 0;
    while (g <= GOLDEN) {
        var s : u8 = t27_status(g);
        if (s == ST_PRESENT) { present = present + 1; }
        if (s == ST_PARTIAL) { partial = partial + 1; }
        if (s == ST_MISSING) { missing = missing + 1; }
        g = g + 1;
    }
    assert present == 1;
    assert partial == 8;
    assert missing == 1;
    assert t27_status(10) == ST_PARTIAL;
    assert t27_status(6) == ST_PARTIAL;
    assert t27_status(1) == ST_MISSING;
    assert golden_filter(7) == C8;
    assert golden_filter(9) == C10;
    assert value(T27C, golden_filter(7)) == TRUE3;
}

; G6 carries two filters: warmup (C6) and speed and quality (C7).
pub fn golden_covers(g: u32, f: u32) -> bool {
    if (golden_filter(g) == f) { return true; }
    if (g == 6) {
        if (f == C7) { return true; }
    }
    return false;
}

test t742_every_filter_is_a_golden_property {
    var f : u32 = 1;
    var covered : u32 = 0;
    while (f <= FILTERS) {
        var g : u32 = 1;
        var hit : bool = false;
        while (g <= GOLDEN) {
            if (golden_covers(g, f)) { hit = true; }
            g = g + 1;
        }
        if (hit) { covered = covered + 1; }
        f = f + 1;
    }
    assert covered == FILTERS;
    assert golden_covers(6, C7);
    assert golden_covers(7, C7) == false;
}
